themes.title: Far-right push for 'national priority' policies
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties across Europe continue to advocate for policies that prioritize nationals over immigrants in access to social benefits, housing, and employment. This theme has intensified in Spain, Italy, Sweden, and Norway, with parties like Vox, Fratelli d'Italia, Sverigedemokraterna, and Fremskrittspartiet leading the charge. The framing often ties immigration to economic strain and cultural preservation, resonating strongly in local and regional governance debates.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Pressures regional governments in Valencia and Mallorca to implement 'national priority' in housing and social aid, tying it to budget negotiations.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Meloni's government secures EU flexibility for energy policies but faces criticism for not extending 'national priority' measures beyond symbolic gestures.

countries.name: 🇸🇪 Sverigedemokraterna
countries.note: Proposes stricter residency requirements for social benefits and housing, framing it as a response to 'welfare tourism'.

countries.name: 🇳🇴 Fremskrittspartiet
countries.note: Advocates for prioritizing Norwegian citizens in public housing and social services, citing integration challenges.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: Jordan Bardella pushes for 'national preference' in employment and welfare, linking it to post-PSG riot discourse on immigration.

themes.title: Javier Milei’s declining approval amid internal strife
themes.blurb: Argentina's President Javier Milei faces growing internal divisions within his La Libertad Avanza coalition, particularly with key figures like Patricia Bullrich and Karina Milei. His approval ratings have dipped below 40% as economic policies spark backlash, and his government grapples with judicial controversies and public protests. International media and domestic critics highlight his erratic leadership style and policy reversals.

themes.title: Far-right gains in European local elections
themes.blurb: Far-right parties are making significant inroads in local and regional elections across Europe, often leveraging anti-immigration and anti-establishment rhetoric. In Germany, the AfD is surging in eastern states, while in Spain, Vox is consolidating power through coalition deals with the PP. Similar trends are observed in Sweden and Italy, where right-wing parties are reshaping municipal governance.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega

themes.title: Internal divisions within far-right parties
themes.blurb: Far-right parties across Europe and the Americas are grappling with internal fractures, often over leadership, policy direction, or personal rivalries. In Argentina, La Libertad Avanza faces public clashes between Milei and Bullrich. In Poland, PiS is divided over its Kraków mayoral candidate. Similar tensions are evident in Hungary's Fidesz/Tisza split and France's RN leadership race.

themes.title: Far-right reactions to Middle East conflicts
themes.blurb: Right-wing and far-right parties are increasingly framing their foreign policy stances through the lens of Middle East conflicts, particularly the Israel-Palestine issue. In the U.S., MAGA-aligned figures criticize Biden's Iran policy, while in Europe, parties like Fratelli d'Italia and Vox express unwavering support for Israel. Poland's PiS and Hungary's Fidesz/Tisza navigate complex relationships with both Israel and Ukraine.
